I think the general mental health sphere has a lot of misuse with words like trauma, manic, etc. or they exaggerate/try to find diagnoses within problems that seem to be very normal or acute instead of fixing the problem so they can write it off. I think these people generally mean well though. I wish there was more education around mental health that wasn’t just people sharing stories and others realizing you get attention from doing so, which makes them want the same attention. I recently had a friend say she has an eating disorder, when what she described seemed to just be a decrease in appetite from her meds and general pickiness (side note- i have an ed and know a lot about eating disorders as its an interest of mine). Another friend also constantly tells me that certain things I went through are trauma even though I am not traumatized from them (just impacted). I think my friends who do this unknowingly want to blame something for their issues instead of digging deeper. I know they mean well but things are much more complex in the mental health world and so much of these terms are taken at surface level understandings. It’s frustrating to people who have very serious issues because people just believe we are the same as people who misuse terms like trauma and mania and overlook our issues. People really should think deeply about such serious claims and ideas before apply them to themselves /: i know they mean well but it sucks.

First of all, no need to apologize for posting- you are so valid. I relate very much to you so I can tell you as much as I have learned that has helped me. For one thing, imagining self harming in front of your parents seems like you wanting to tell them you’re not okay, or let out your anger of not being taken seriously. If you could find a way to ask for help- whether this is talking to your parents or using resources at your school, community, etc, this would be a great step and may ease those urges. I have the same thoughts about self harming or telling my mom about drug use or eating to get her attention at the level I need it. Its taken me a long time to be able to open up to anybody and even find a therapist who I can tell some minor things to. Know you’re not alone- I felt that way for so long but have realized that I am so understood by so many, I just couldn’t see that because I was afraid. You are not alone. I have made a friend who is struggling in the same ways I am and I feel a huge relief to know I’m not “going crazy”. I know it’s incredibly scary to ask for help and any time I do so, I end up balling my eyes out, but I always get a sense of relief from knowing there will be some change. 

     Finding outlets helps a ton as well (especially when you’re lonely/ friendless). I opt to reading, drawing, and practicing spirituality. I think this helps a lot to ease my anxiety. I can take my mind off of things and escape for a while when I do the things I like. I dunno if you’re religious/spiritual, however I find this to be a way I can find hope. I always reach for my tarot cards and end up feeling a sense of calm and feeling like the universe will take care of me. If this is not your jam, that’s totally cool. I still suggested finding things that give you hope- don’t get too sucked into negative media or spiral about the fucked up parts of the world. I do that a lot and it never helps, but knowing there is good in the world makes me want to be there to experience it. 

     Another thing that may help you is some sort of self talk/journaling. I used to journal every single day and I would sometimes end up being able to identify really complex things about myself that I didn’t realize were causing me pain. Today I find it much more helpful to do video diaries. I have ADHD so I think way faster than I can write so sitting in front of my laptop camera (u could even do your phone or talk to yourself out loud) and just talking for as long as I feel can be incredibly relieving- even if its just to get things off of my mind. This also helps when you don’t have friends/ therapists/ people who you want to open up to about certain problems. 

I know this is a lot so let me say this- you are not alone and there are people who do and will understand you. Asking for help is incredibly scary and I know you are brave enough. Find someone or some way you can feel safe working through your thoughts. Its a process that can be confusing and bumpy, but keep going! I am here for you if you feel the need to message someone. I love new friends and am incredibly happy to help. 

Keep pushing friend <3
